## Install from AgentForge Labs R-universe

Package installation is free. Hosted API usage requires an AgentForge/SnapForge
account and is metered server-side. The SDK never disables or bypasses quota
enforcement.

```r
install.packages(
  "snapforge",
  repos = c(
    "https://agentforge-labs.r-universe.dev",
    "https://cloud.r-project.org"
  )
)
```

Create a free account in the SnapForge web application, create an API key, and
store it outside source code:

```r
Sys.setenv(SNAPFORGE_API_KEY = "replace-with-your-key")
library(snapforge)
client <- snapforge_client()
```

Capture a page and inspect quota metadata:

```r
capture <- snapforge_capture(
  client,
  "https://example.com",
  device = "both",
  idempotency_key = "my-stable-request-id"
)
capture$body$files
capture$quota
```

Read page context:

```r
context <- snapforge_context(client, "https://example.com")
context$body$context$summary
```

Persisted job helpers are available for status and artifacts:

```r
job <- snapforge_get_job(client, capture$body$jobId)
archive <- snapforge_download_job(client, capture$body$jobId)
```

## Explicit self-hosted mode

Self-hosted/community deployments are never selected implicitly. Point the
client at them explicitly:

```r
local <- snapforge_client(
  base_url = "http://localhost:3010",
  access_token = ""
)
snapforge_service_info(local)
```

URL-secret authentication is also supported for compatible deployments:

```r
secret_client <- snapforge_client(
  base_url = "https://screenshots.example.com",
  access_token = "",
  url_secret = Sys.getenv("SNAPFORGE_URL_SECRET")
)
```

## Forward-compatible public API calls

Compatible additive public endpoints can be used before a typed helper ships:

```r
snapforge_request(
  client,
  "/api/v1/future-compatible-endpoint",
  method = "POST",
  body = list(example = TRUE),
  idempotency_key = "future-1"
)
```

The raw request path still applies authentication, timeout, idempotency,
structured errors, and credential redaction, and rejects private/admin paths.

## Errors and quota

HTTP failures raise a `snapforge_http_error`. The condition carries
`status`, redacted `body`, and `quota` fields:

```r
tryCatch(
  snapforge_capture(client, "https://example.com"),
  snapforge_http_error = function(err) {
    print(err$status)
    print(err$quota)
  }
)
```
